title: Check real original OpenArt MP4 stream dimensions before padded frames and AI verification
root_cause: Netlify's original frame extractor always converted any aspect ratio into padded 1080x1920 JPEGs. The downstream router called AI face/temporal verification on these derived frames and accepted caller-supplied frames without independent original native MP4 stream verification. The OpenArt Kling original was 1292x1604, but generated JPEG was padded to 1080x1920, causing irrelevant frame-face failures.

evidence.source_provenance: OpenArt media metadata + production router and Netlify source readback

prevention_rule: Before generating any image comparison, independently inspect original MP4 first stream dimensions via ffmpeg, reject or quarantine every non-native / unknown stream, record immutable rejected history in original Brain+CAS job, never trust padded JPEG or caller frames, and then allow only fresh original-master source-locked correctly-sized history subject to provider budget. Existing 0.940 face/0.900 temporal and Meta provider proof remain mandatory.
fix: Introduce native-MP4 stream probe in original Netlify extractor, require every Reel router submission to use extracted original-byte frames with native 1080x1920 proof before vision, write real mismatches to existing CAS/Brain and provide failure-specific next-generation action in original Mira producer plan.
outcome: Candidate PR only until exact-head Required, CodeQL, native Supabase/Netlify preview, protected merge and independently deployed sources; not evidence of new published Reel or revenue.
